description: BioHealth es un equipo que tiene como objetivo principal llevar a la práctica los conocimientos adquiridos durante la carrera universitaria.
summary: We developed a health monitoring software that tracks vital signs, mood, and clinical emergencies from the different members of a certain mission crew. The program is able to analyze the input data and deliver alerts whenever it notices abnormal or unhealthy records. Emergency and preventive protocols were added so that astronauts in long missions can take care of their own and their crew's health.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

Before the mission begins, it must be recorded along with its crew members in the Basic Crew Information section. A short description of every member is saved and a pre-flight parameter list must be fulfilled.
In order to register data daily, the user must go in the Record Symptoms or data section, click on the body map buttons and input the required information in every slot. When necessary, the user can guide themselves by the sensors previously used on missions, which will deliver the necessary details. Whenever an anomaly is detected, either an emergency or preventive protocol is automatically activated.
Every anomaly, along with the carried out protocol, is stored to be sent to the land-based base.

What benefits does it have?

The user-friendly interface allows the astronauts to be autonomous in the recording and interpretation of their physiological signs. Added to that, the alerts help have a quick response to emergencies and the reports help keep up-to-date clinical records that support further mission analyses about the health performance in space for future developments.

What is the intended impact of the project?

We seek an improvement in astronauts' safety and autonomy. The software allows them to guard their health, identify possible problems and act quickly on them. Furthermore, it speeds up clinical follow-up through records and downloadable briefings.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

The entirety of the code for the Software was developed in Visual Studio Code, using Python as the base programming language (streamlit library) and CSS for aesthetic retouches. The background pictures were taken from Pinterest and the body map was drawn by a member of the team.

How is your project creative?

Instead of a long and boring questionnaire, the user must only touch one of the proposed body parts and register the symptoms and signs indicated. Besides, every emergency protocol is read out loud, giving time and availability to the astronauts during the eventuality so they do not have to read, just listen and follow the instructions. For prevention protocols, the integrated exercise routines and general recommendations help astronauts focus on indirect aspects of their health.

What factors did your team consider?

We focused on the main affections reported on the NASA literature and based our recordings on the ones of the Bio-Monitor created by the Canadian Space Agency. Besides, we used the detailed physiological limits on the analysis of the input data along with succesful registered countermeasures for every case.

We considered the interactivity and easiness of use, with simple language so that no misunderstangings can be made for the users.
